judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fixed 25-cent bonus tied to an identified machine with an express carve-out for walk trucks; nothing to construe.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It creates two different lists (seniority and priority) in one sentence and then says only the seniority list governs layoff, leaving priority's basis unstated here.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Depends entirely on 4-A.1's regular-situation-holder list; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short transitional rule keyed to the most recent published lists.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short introductory grant of a right, with the limitations set out in the following subparagraphs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A regular day's work shall consist of 7 hours and 54 minutes or less' defines work by duration while the same sentence names a twelve-hour window as 'the day shift', so 'shift' carries two senses in one line.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It defines short nights, one long night and a Saturday night with different lengths and two different starting hours, all lumped together as 'the night shift' — the term does not have a single referent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 13-H.1 and 13-I.1 compute contributions 'per shift for each shift worked' and cap them at five shifts a week, and 5-D distributes the night week over five nights, so the definition here determines Fund liability.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The weekly hours figure is rendered '8915', so the numeric limit is not legible from the text as written.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5-A's 7 hours 54 minutes over five days yields 39.5 hours, and 5-F defines overtime by reference to these limits, so the intended figure is recoverable from the rest.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 36½-hour weekly figure is rendered '8644', and the clause enumerates five nights while calling only one 'long'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short pay-guarantee sentence keyed to 'each regular day's work or ... regular night's work'.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: 13-D fixes the overtime rate and five-minute computation, 5-J prices unnoticed starting-time changes at time and one-half, and 22-D(vi) gives benefit credit for 45 hours without a fifth shift.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'So that as many regular situations as possible may be created and maintained' is an unmeasurable obligation on its face.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5-K pays time and one-half for Sunday work generally and 5-I double time for advance sections, so three overlapping Sunday premiums coexist.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5-K prescribes time and one-half for Sunday work in exactly the same 10:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. window, so the two rates compete for the same hours.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The penalty sentence is convoluted ('the time involved in the change from the time of notice for four (4) days'), leaving the quantum of pay uncertain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single, precise premium rate for a defined Sunday window.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5-I sets double time for advance-section work in the identical window and 5-H double time for certain Sunday evening-paper work, so the rate for a given Sunday hour is contested.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Sufficiently far from where it began to involve substantial travel time' is doubly vague and the clause then defers the arrangement to future negotiation.
